parts.text:
Identify the trend in the number of students moving to a different country for university, from
Source 1.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify two benefits of moving to a different country, from Source 2.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Which benefit of moving to a different country do you think is most important? Explain why.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Explain why young people moving to a different country is an important national issue.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
‘Young people do not care about their culture.’
What are the strengths and weaknesses of the argument supporting this claim?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
‘Students who study in a different country have more interest in other cultures.’
How would you test this claim? You should consider the types of information, sources of
evidence or methods you might use.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify one opinion in Nikita’s statement.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify one prediction in Tanu’s statement.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why Nikita’s statement might be biased.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Which argument is more convincing, Nikita’s or Tanu’s?
Your answer should consider both statements and you should support your point of view with
their words.
You should also consider:
• the strength of their reasoning and evidence
• their use of language
• the different types of information used.

text: ‘Young people should not move away to study because their local communities will suffer.’
Do you agree with this statement?
• give reasons and evidence to support your opinion
• use the material in the sources and/or any of your own ideas
